titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 22 and the rubric of Spell 72
part: Spell 22 and the rubric of Spell 72 (Plate 6)
about: Spell 22 is a spell for giving a mouth to the dead: the Osiris Ani, risen like the sun from the egg in the hidden land, asks for his mouth so that he may speak with it before the great god, the lord of the Duat, says he has come from the Pool of Flame and quenched it, and hails the lord of light, foremost of the Mansion. On the papyrus it follows Spell 1 on Plate 6, and the scribe goes straight on to the rubric of Spell 72, the closing instructions of another spell, given here without that spell's own words. The rubric promises that whoever knows the writing and has it put on his coffin will go forth by day in any form he wishes, eat at the altar of Osiris and live in the Field of Reeds. This part runs from Plate 6, line 1 of Spell 22, to line 7 of the rubric, in Budge's numbering, which starts again at each.

sentences.l: spell · of · giving · a-mouth · to · the-Osiris · the-scribe · accountant · of-the-god's-offerings · of-gods · all · Ani · true-of-voice · to-him · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for giving a mouth to the Osiris, the accounting scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, true of voice, (giving it) to him in the necropolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the title in red, except Ani's name and titles from wsir to mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, which are black; the red takes up again with n·f (Budge marks the red with a line over the hieroglyphs). Budge's line numerals start again at 1 with this spell. rꜣ n 'spell for' is the mouth rꜣ with its stroke and the genitive n, the heading of every chapter. rdit 'giving' is the mouth r, the giving arm di and t: the infinitive of rdi. In Budge's type the arm lacks its loaf; it is coded D37 as the word requires. rꜣ n 'a mouth to': the mouth again, now the thing given, and n 'to', the dative. Wsir N 'the Osiris N' (the seat, Q2, approximate, and the eye) is the title of the dead man, who hopes to live again as the god did. sš ḥsb 'accounting scribe' (the palette, the sign ḥsb, coded Aa2, approximate, and the roll) is Ani's title as in Spell 1. Budge's groups neter and ḥetepu are joined as one word, ḥtp-nṯr 'god's offerings': the flag nṯr, written first out of respect and standing in Budge's square brackets (restored where the papyrus is damaged), then the offering table ḥtp with t and p as complements. nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods': the flag with a seated god and a stroke, and the basket nb with plural strokes. ꜣny 'Ani' has a seated man as classifier (A1). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth and the oar, without the sickle. Budge prints mꜣꜥ-ḫrw and n·f as one group; they are two words, and only n·f is red. n·f 'to him' (water n and the viper ·f, whose horns Budge's type prints as a small cross beside it, as in Spell 1) takes up the name again after the long titles. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is written as in Spell 1: the loop taken as r (coded D21, approximate), the flag nṯr and the sign ẖr in one ligature. To 'give a mouth' is to restore the power of speech, which the dead need to say their spells.

sentences.l: said(?) · am-I · risen · from · the-egg · which-is-in · the-land · hidden
sentences.i: Said(?): I have risen from the egg which is in the hidden land.
sentences.n: The speech begins, in black. Its first word is doubtful. Budge reads T'eṭṭu, 'to be said', but his type shows only the cobra ḏ, drawn tall, with a stroke over three plural strokes; the hand d that should follow the cobra in ḏd 'say' is not printed. It is read ḏd 'said' here, perhaps for ḏd mdw 'words spoken', the usual head of a recitation, with mdw left out; the reading is doubtful. iw·i is the reed i and the chick w with ·i, the seated man; Budge's line numeral 2 is printed among the signs. Budge's two groups uben and kuà are joined here as one word: wbn·kwi 'I have risen' is the chick w, the foot b and water n with the sun as classifier, the verb wbn 'rise, shine' said of the sun, then the basket k, the chick w and the seated man, the ending ·kwi of the stative, 'I'. iw·i with the stative states a condition: 'I am risen, I have risen'. swḥt 'egg' is the folded cloth s, w, the wick ḥ and t with an egg as classifier. imyt 'which is in' is the crossed planks im with m as complement and t: the nisba of m 'in', feminine to agree with swḥt, its y not written. tꜣ štꜣ 'the hidden land': the strip of land tꜣ, then the pool š, t, a small cup (coded W10, approximate) that is not read, the vulture ꜣ, a small cross and the roll, as štꜣw is written in Spell 1. The dead man speaks as the sun god, born from an egg at the beginning of things.

sentences.l: is-given · to-me · mouth-my · may-speak-I · with-it · before · the-god · great · lord · of-the-Duat
sentences.i: My mouth is given to me, so that I may speak with it before the great god, the lord of the Duat.
sentences.n: iw 'is' (reed and chick) opens the statement and is not translated. Budge's group erṭāu-nà is divided here into two words: rdi·w is the mouth r, the giving arm di (again printed without its loaf and coded D37) and the chick w, the passive sḏm·f of rdi 'give' with the w it sometimes shows; n·i 'to me' is water n and ·i. Budge's line numeral 3 is printed inside the group. With iw the passive states what is so: 'is given'; Budge takes it as a wish ('may be given'), which the passive also allows. rꜣ·i 'my mouth' is the mouth with its stroke and ·i, the subject placed after the dative. ḏdw·i 'that I may speak' begins with a tall narrow sign coded U28 (approximate), which stands for ḏ as in Spell 1 and the introduction to Spell 125; then the hand d, the chick w, the man with hand to mouth (the classifier of speech) and ·i. The w marks the prospective sḏm·f, used after another verb for purpose: 'so that I may speak'. im·f 'with it' is the reed and the owl m, the form of m before a suffix, with ·f; the small cross printed with the viper is its horns. m-bꜣḥ 'before, in the presence of' is the owl m and the phallus bꜣḥ with the roll. nṯr ꜥꜣ 'the great god': the flag with a seated god, the column ꜥꜣ with the arm ꜥ as complement and the roll. nb dwꜣt 'lord of the Duat': the basket nb, then the star dwꜣ with the vulture ꜣ as complement, t and an open house sign as classifier (coded O1 from its shape; Budge: ṭuat). Budge's numeral 4 stands between the star and the rest. The great god is Osiris, ruler of the world below.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-repelled · arm-my · by · the-tribunal · of · god · any
sentences.i: My arm shall not be repelled by the tribunal of any god.
sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms of negation (D35) alone, before the passive sḏm·tw·f. ḫsf·tw 'is repelled' is the spindle with the viper joined to it (U35), a single sign for ḫsf, with an arm as classifier of force (coded D40, approximate), then t and w, the tw of the passive. Here the subject is a noun, ꜥ·i 'my arm', the arm ꜥ with its stroke and ·i, so no suffix follows tw. As in Spell 1, n with this form among the speaker's wishes is taken for the future, 'shall not be repelled'; the past ('was not repelled') is also possible. m 'by' brings in the agent. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'tribunal, council' is written as in Spell 1: the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) twice, a small ring with a nub (coded W24) between them that is not read, t, and as classifiers a bar with ticks (coded N1, approximate), plural strokes and a seated god. n nṯr nb 'of any god': the genitive n, the flag with a seated god and nb 'every, any' after its noun. The tribunals of the gods judged the dead; the arm stands for the power to act.

sentences.l: I · Osiris · lord · of-Rosetau
sentences.i: I am Osiris, lord of Rosetau.
sentences.n: ink 'I' is the pot nw (for in), the basket k and the seated man; ink with a noun is 'I am …'. wsir is the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye: here the god himself, whose part the speaker takes. nb rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'lord of Rosetau': the basket nb, then the mouth rꜣ with a stroke, the drag-rope sṯꜣ (V2), a stroke, plural strokes and the desert-hill sign (N25), as Rosetau is written in Spell 1. Budge's numeral 5 is printed between the mouth and the rope. Rosetau, the realm of Sokar in the Memphite cemetery, was where the body of Osiris was said to lie.

sentences.l: shares · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · with · this-one · who-is · upon · the-stairs
sentences.i: The Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, has a share with the one who is on top of the stairs.
sentences.n: The speech goes on in the third person, as the papyrus often does. psš 'share, divide' is the stool p, the bolt s and the pool š, with a small cross and a tall roll as classifiers: the sḏm·f, 'he shares', with the noun subject after it. Wsir sš ꜣny 'the Osiris, the scribe Ani': the seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye, the palette sš, and Ani's name with a man seated on a chair holding a flail (A51). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' has the man with hand to mouth after the oar. m 'with': psš m is to share in or with. nn 'this, these' is water n, the adze nw (U19), the pot nw and the chick w, the demonstrative as in Spell 1, here standing alone as a noun, 'this one'. nty 'who is' is water n, t and two strokes y, the relative adjective. The papyrus writes tp·f, the head tp with its stroke and the viper f (Budge marks it '(sic)'); read tp 'upon, on top of', as in tp tꜣ 'upon earth'. The viper (its horns printed as a small cross) has no place here. ḫt 'stairs' is the placenta ḫ and t with a stairway as classifier (O40): the word for a flight of steps or a terrace (Budge: χet, 'steps'), not otherwise met in the published parts. The one on top of the stairs is the god enthroned at the head of his stairway, Osiris as judge.

sentences.l: have-come-I · according-to · the-desire · of-heart-my · from · the-Pool · of-Flame · have-quenched-I
sentences.i: I have come as my heart desired from the Pool of Flame, and I have quenched (it).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this sentence in red. ii·n·i 'I have come' is the reed-pair ii (M18) with the reed i as complement, walking legs, then n of the sḏm·n·f, the form for a completed action, and ·i. r 'according to' is the mouth r. mrr 'the desire' is the hoe mr with r as complement, a second r, and the man with hand to mouth: the doubled stem of mri 'love, wish', used as a noun, 'what (my heart) desires'; r mrr ib·i is 'as my heart wished'. ib·i 'my heart' is the heart with its stroke and ·i. m 'from'. The next two words are doubtful. š 'pool' is the pool sign with a small sign under it like two bars joined by crossing lines (coded N23, approximate) and a stroke. Then come two flames on braziers (Q7), t and a round town sign (coded O49); Budge reads nesert 'fire'. It is read nsrt 'flame' here, the first brazier writing nsr and the second taken as a classifier; the doubled sign may instead stand for a doubled stem, nsrsr, and the reading is not sure. š nsrt is 'the Pool of Flame', a place of the world below. ꜥḫm·n·i 'I have quenched' is the arm ꜥ, the placenta ḫ and the owl m, with a brazier as classifier, n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i, as in the address of Spell 125; Budge's numeral 7 is printed inside it. Its object, the fire, is not written. The dead man has come through the fire that guards the way and has put it out.

sentences.l: greetings-to-your-face · lord · of-light · foremost · of-the-Mansion · chief(?) · of-darkness · deep(?)
sentences.i: Hail to you, lord of light, foremost of the Mansion, chief(?) of the deep(?) darkness!
sentences.n: Budge prints ind ḥr·k 'hail to you' as one group, and so it is kept here as one word: the reed i and the sign nḏ (coded Aa27) begin it, then the face ḥr with its stroke, and only after the face the cobra ḏ, the complement of nḏ, and the roll that belong to ind; ·k 'you' closes the group. Literally 'greetings to your face', as in the hymns and Spell 1. sšp 'light' is the sign šsp (O42) with p as complement and the sun as classifier; Budge reads seśep 'radiance'. The signs give šsp; the word for light and brightness is sšp, with an s that is not written here, so the reading is doubtful. ḫnty 'foremost of' is the jar-stand ḫnt with n and t as complements and two strokes y, the nisba used of Osiris (ḫnty imntt). ḥwt 'the Mansion' is the enclosure ḥwt with t and a house sign. The next word is doubtful: the face ḥr over the mouth r, t, then the head tp with a stroke and a seated god (Budge: ḥert, 'Great'). It is read ḥry-tp 'chief, who is at the head', a title, with the god sign as classifier of a divine person; the t, which would make the word feminine to agree with ḥwt, is not read. kkw 'darkness' is two baskets k and the chick w with the sky sign hung with a sceptre (N2), the classifier of night, and a stroke. smꜣw is the lung-and-windpipe smꜣ (F36) with ꜣ, w, the roll and a stroke; Budge's numeral 8 follows the first sign. smꜣ means 'unite, join', and kkw smꜣw is taken as 'deep, unbroken darkness'; the sense is not sure. The god hailed is the lord of light who is also master of the darkness: the sun in the world below, or Osiris.

sentences.l: have-come-I · to-you
sentences.i: I have come to you.
sentences.n: The speech goes on in black. ii·n·i 'I have come', the sḏm·n·f, written as in the red line. ḫr·k 'to you' is the placenta ḫ, the mouth r and ·k: ḫr is 'to, near', used of coming into the presence of a person.

sentences.l: am-glorious-I · am-pure-I
sentences.i: I am glorious, I am pure.
sentences.n: Two statives with the ending ·kwi 'I'. Budge's groups χu-k and [uà] are joined here as one word, ꜣḫ·kwi 'I am glorious, effective': the crested ibis ꜣḫ with the placenta ḫ as complement and the roll, then the basket k; the chick w and the seated man that complete the ending stand in Budge's square brackets and are restored where the papyrus is damaged. wꜥb·kwi 'I am pure' is the vase pouring water over a foot (D60), the word-sign wꜥb, with water (N35A) as classifier, and k, w and the seated man. To be an ꜣḫ, an effective spirit, and to be pure are what the dead must be to stand before the god.

sentences.l: arms-my · about-you
sentences.i: My two arms are about you.
sentences.n: ꜥwy·i 'my two arms' is the arm ꜥ with a stroke, a second arm, the chick w and two strokes y, and ·i: the dual of ꜥ, written as in the introduction to Spell 125. ḥꜣ·k 'behind you, about you' is a stalk with buds (M16, ḥꜣ) with the vulture ꜣ as complement, a small head sign as classifier (coded D1; the back of the head), and ·k. A noun with a preposition makes a sentence without a verb. The gesture is the one of protection, arms placed behind or around the god, as Isis and Nephthys stand behind Osiris.

sentences.l: portion-your · ancestors-your
sentences.i: Your portion is (that of) your ancestors(?).
sentences.n: The sentence is doubtful. dni·k is the hand d, water n and the reed i, with a vertical stroke joined to a crescent (coded Aa16, approximate) and ·k; Budge reads ṭenà-k 'thy portion'. A noun dni 'share, portion' is taken here; the classifier cannot be identified with certainty. tpyw-ꜥ·k 'your ancestors' is the head tp with its stroke and the stool p as complement, the chick w, the arm ꜥ with a stroke, a squatting man holding a flail (A52) and plural strokes, and ·k: tpyw-ꜥ, literally 'those who were before', the forebears. The two nouns stand side by side with no verb or preposition between them; Budge supplies '[is with]'. The translation keeps what stands and marks the doubt. The ancestors are the blessed dead who went before into the world below.

sentences.l: may-give-you · to-me · mouth-my · may-speak-I · with-it
sentences.i: May you give me my mouth, that I may speak with it.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this sentence in red: the request at the heart of the spell. di·k is the giving arm di and ·k: the sḏm·f of rdi used as a wish, 'may you give', with the force of a request. n·i 'to me', rꜣ·i 'my mouth', ḏdw·i 'that I may speak' (the tall ḏ coded U28, approximate, the hand d, w, the man with hand to mouth and ·i, the prospective sḏm·f of purpose) and im·f 'with it' are written as in line 3. The mouth is asked for so that the spells can be spoken.

sentences.l: may-follow-I · heart-my · at · hour-its · of-flame(?) · and-night
sentences.i: May I follow my heart at its hour of flame(?) and of night.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ib without the seated man ·i; read ib·i 'my heart', as Budge does (àb-à). The first word is doubtful: the bolt s, a low sign on legs with a hooked end (coded T18, approximate), the owl m, the roll and ·i (Budge: sem-à, 'may I follow'). T18 is the sign šms 'follow', with m as its complement; the s may stand for its last consonant written first. It is read šms·i, a sḏm·f wish, but the identification of the sign is not sure. n 'at' (water n) is the preposition. wnwt·f 'its hour' is the hare wn with n, the pot nw, t, the star, the sun and a stroke, as wnwt is written in the address of Spell 125, then the viper ·f, its horns printed as a small cross. The next word is doubtful too: water n, the foot b, the hand d and t with a brazier as classifier (Budge: nebṭet, 'of fire'). It is read nbdt, some word for flame or burning, from its classifier only. grḥ 'night' is the stand g, the mouth r and the wick ḥ with the sky and sceptre (N2) as classifier. nbdt and grḥ stand side by side, both after wnwt·f; 'and' is supplied. To follow one's heart is to do as one wishes.

sentences.l: if · is-known · writing · this · upon · earth · is-put-it · in · writing · upon · the-coffin · spell-my(?) · it-is
sentences.i: If this writing is known upon earth, and it is put in writing upon the coffin — it is my spell(?) —
sentences.n: The rubric of Spell 72 follows directly; Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes it in red from rḫ to sp in line 7, except wsir in line 3 and the nine flags in line 6; the first word, ir, is black. ir 'if' (reed i, mouth r) heads a condition. rḫ 'is known' (r, ḫ, the roll) is the passive sḏm·f, its subject after it. šꜥt 'writing, document' is written as in the rubric of Spell 125, without the pool š or the arm ꜥ: the papyrus roll with its tie, t and a stroke, and a loop with crossing tails (coded V6, approximate) as classifier. The reading follows Budge (śāt); the roll with t and stroke is also the regular writing of mḏꜣt 'book', which fits the signs as well. tn 'this' (t, water n) is feminine, after its noun. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': the head with its stroke and the strip of land. ir·tw·s 'it is put' stands in Budge's square brackets and is restored: the eye ir, t and w, the passive sḏm·tw·f of iri, and the bolt ·s 'it', the writing. m sš 'in writing': the palette with the roll and a stroke. ḥr qrsw 'upon the coffin': the face ḥr with its stroke, then the hill-slope q, r and the bolt s, with a long coffin shape (coded Q6, approximate) and an L-shaped box (coded D40, approximate) as classifiers; qrsw 'coffin' is from qrs 'bury', its w not written. rꜣ·i pw 'it is my spell': the mouth with its stroke and ·i, then pw (stool p, chick w), 'it is'. The ·i makes little sense in a rubric that speaks of the dead man as 'he', and Budge's footnote suggests reading rꜣ pn 'this spell'; the translation keeps what stands and marks the doubt. A rubric says how a spell is to be used and what it gives.

sentences.l: will-go-forth-he · by · day · in · forms · all · wishes-he
sentences.i: he will go forth by day in every form he wishes
sentences.n: iw·f pr·f 'he will go forth' is iw with ·f followed by the sḏm·f pr·f: iw·f sḏm·f states what happens as a rule, and in a rubric's promise it is put in English as 'he will …'. In iw·f, as in every ·f of this part, the viper's horns are printed as a small cross beside it. pr·f is the house pr with r as complement and walking legs. m hrw 'by day': m is the sign Aa15 here, and hrw is the courtyard h, r, the chick w, the sun and a stroke. pr m hrw 'going forth by day' is what the whole book is named for. m ḫprw nb 'in every form': ḫprw 'forms, manifestations' is the scarab ḫpr with r, w, a mummy-shaped seated figure (A53) and the roll and a stroke as classifiers. mr·f 'he wishes' is the canal sign mr (N36) with its stroke and ·f: the verb mri 'love, wish' written with a sign of the same sound, a relative form, '(which) he wishes', after its noun. To take any form at will is one of the powers the spells promise.

sentences.l: and · going-in · to · the-place · not · shall-be-turned-back-he
sentences.i: and go in to (his) place; he shall not be turned back.
sentences.n: ḥnꜥ 'with, and' is the wick ḥ, water n and the arm ꜥ; with an infinitive after it, it adds a second action: ḥnꜥ ꜥq 'and going in'. ꜥq 'go in' is the bird ꜥq with q as complement (the hill-slope, printed as a small triangle) and walking legs. r st 'to the place': st is the seat st with t and a house sign. Budge supplies '[his]'; no suffix is written. n 'not' is the arms of negation with water n as complement. šnꜥ·tw·f 'he shall be turned back' is the loop šn with n, the arm ꜥ, a recumbent lion (E23), which is not read, walking legs, then t and w of the passive and ·f, written as in Spell 1. As there, n with this form is taken for the future. Guardians at the gates of the world below turn back the unworthy dead.

sentences.l: is-given · to-him · bread · beer · a-great-portion · of · meat · upon · the-altar · of · Osiris
sentences.i: Bread and beer and a great portion of meat shall be given to him upon the altar of Osiris.
sentences.n: iw di·tw n·f 'there is given to him': iw, then di·tw, the giving arm di with t and w, the passive sḏm·tw·f of rdi, with the things given after the dative n·f. t 'bread' is t with two loaves as classifiers, a truncated-cone mould (coded X2, approximate) and a long rounded loaf (X4), and a stroke; Budge reads ta, 'cakes'. ḥnqt 'beer' is the beer jug alone with a stroke, a word-sign; the jug is drawn like a small tied pot (coded W22, approximate). wr n iwf 'a great portion of meat': wr is the swallow wr with r as complement, 'a great amount', joined to iwf by the genitive n; Budge renders ur 'meat', but the swallow writes wr 'great'. iwf 'meat' is the reed i, the chick w and the viper f (its horns printed as a small cross). ḥr ḫꜣwt 'upon the altar': ḫꜣwt is a bowl on a pedestal with loaves (R1), the word-sign, with t and a stroke. nt 'of' is water n and t, the feminine genitive agreeing with ḫꜣwt. wsir, written here with the eye above the tall seat and the seated god, is black in the red rubric, the god's name set apart. The altar of Osiris is where offerings to the god were laid, and the dead man is to share them.

sentences.l: will-go-in-he · in · peace · to · the-Field-of-Reeds
sentences.i: He will go in in peace to the Field of Reeds
sentences.n: iw·f ꜥq·f 'he will go in', iw·f sḏm·f as in line 1, with ꜥq written as in line 2. m ḥtp 'in peace': the offering table ḥtp with t and p as complements. r 'to'. sḫt-iꜣrw 'the Field of Reeds' (Budge: Seχet-Àaru) is the field sign sḫt (M20) with t, a small triangle under it (coded N21, approximate), then the reed i, the vulture ꜣ, the mouth r and the chick w, with a plant of three stems (coded M15, approximate), plural strokes and a town sign as classifiers. The vulture is written here, where the hymn to Osiris leaves it out. The Field of Reeds is the fertile land of the blessed dead, where they sow and reap.

sentences.l: in-order-to · know · command · this · of · the-one-who-is-in(?) · Busiris
sentences.i: to know this command of the one who is in(?) Busiris.
sentences.n: r with an infinitive is 'in order to': r rḫ 'to know'. wḏ 'command' is the wḏ sign (coded V24) with the chick w as complement and the roll: the noun from wḏ 'command', masculine with pn 'this' (stool p, water n) after it. n 'of'. imyt 'the one who is in' is the crossed planks im with m as complement and t: the nisba of m, here feminine. Budge renders 'the [one] in'; the feminine t may point to a goddess, or may be written without regard to gender, and who is meant is not sure. ḏdw 'Busiris' (Budge: Ṭeṭṭeṭ) is the ḏd-pillar twice, the second repeating the first, and the town sign, without the hand d and the chick w of Spell 1; Budge's numeral 5 is printed between the pillars and the town sign. Busiris, in the Delta, was the chief city of Osiris in the north.

sentences.l: is-given · to-him · barley · emmer · in-it
sentences.i: Barley and emmer shall be given to him there.
sentences.n: iw di·tw n·f 'there is given to him', as in line 3. it 'barley' is the grain measure with grain pouring from it (U9), the word-sign, over plural strokes; Budge reads pert 'wheat', but no house sign pr is printed and the measure alone writes it, as in the hymn to Osiris. bdt 'emmer' is the ear of emmer (M34) with t, two strokes and the grain measure with plural strokes as classifiers (Budge: beti, 'barley'). it and bdt, the two chief grains of Egypt, are paired without 'and'. im·s 'in it' is the reed and the owl m with the bolt s, ·s 'it': it refers to the Field (sḫt, feminine). The blessed dead are fed from the harvest of the Field of Reeds.

sentences.l: will-be · with-him · fresh-plants · as · was-he · upon · earth
sentences.i: Fresh green plants shall be his, as when he was upon earth.
sentences.n: wnn 'there will be' is the hare wn with water n twice: the doubled stem of wnn 'be', used for the future. ḫr·f 'with him' (ḫ, r and ·f). wꜣḏ 'fresh plants, greens' is a papyrus stem with a cobra twined round it (M13 and I10 in one ligature), the cobra the complement ḏ, and a stroke; the word also means 'green, flourishing', and 'he will flourish' may be meant. mi 'as, like' is the pot in a net (W19) with the reed. wn·n·f 'he was' is the hare wn with n, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·f: the past of wnn. tp tꜣ 'upon earth'. The life in the Field of Reeds repeats the farmer's life on earth.

sentences.l: will-do-he · what-wishes-he · (n?) · like · this · Ennead · which-is · in · the-Duat
sentences.i: He will do what he wishes, like this Ennead which is in the Duat,
sentences.n: iw·f ir·f 'he will do', iw·f sḏm·f as in line 1: the eye ir with r as complement. mrt·f 'what he wishes' is the hoe mr with r, t, the man with hand to mouth, and ·f: the relative form of mri, 'that which he loves, wishes', as in the address of Spell 125. Water n stands before mi; it has no clear place, and may be a genitive n misplaced from between nn and its noun (nn n X), so it is not translated. mi 'like'. nn 'this, these' is two rushes and two waters, as in Spell 1. Nine gods' flags follow, in black amid the red: nine for the Nine, psḏt 'the Ennead' (Budge reads neteru, 'gods'). The flag is written nine times instead of spelling the word; it is read here as the Ennead, the reading 'the gods' being also possible. nty m dwꜣt 'who are in the Duat': nty (n, t, two strokes) and dwꜣt written with the star, the vulture as complement, t and the open house sign, as in line 3 of Spell 22; Budge's numeral 7 is printed before the star. The Ennead is the company of the great gods, here those of the world below.

sentences.l: in · truly · right · a-million · of · times
sentences.i: truly right, a million times.
sentences.n: m šs mꜣꜥ is a set phrase that closes rubrics: m 'in, as', šs (the cord šs, V6, with a stroke and the roll; Budge: śes, 'bond') and mꜣꜥ 'true, right' (the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ and the roll). šs mꜣꜥ, 'truly right', as at the end of the rubric of Spell 125, vouches that the spell works; the exact sense of šs is not sure. ḥḥ n sp 'a million times': ḥḥ is the god Heh with raised arms (C11), the number a million, with two strokes, and sp 'time, occasion' is the bolt s and the stool p with the threshing-floor sp (O50) as classifier. The phrase claims the method has been tried a million times.

sentences.l: (iw) · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani
sentences.i: The Osiris, the scribe Ani …
sentences.n: The red ends with sp, and these words are black. iw (reed and chick) opens a statement, but no predicate follows before the plate ends with Ani's name; the words may simply set his name at the foot of the rubric. Wsir sš ꜣny 'the Osiris, the scribe Ani': the seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye, the palette, and Ani's name with the man on a chair holding a flail (A51). The heading 'Plate VII' follows in Budge, and with it the next part.
